text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, the mid-process branch after A19/A20 runs through different activities: A21, A22 and A23 each appear in only about 25 in 100 traces, down from about 75 in 100 before (150→51, 151→49 and 150→49 of 200 traces), while A24, A25 and A26 rise from about 26 in 100 to about 76 in 100 (51→153, 52→152, 51→151 traces). [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024]
- The rerouting is visible at the branch point itself. Earlier, A19 was followed by A21/A22/A23 in about 74 in 100 of their joint appearances; later, A19 is followed by A24/A25/A26 in about 75 in 100. A20's outgoing transitions shift in step, from roughly three quarters leading into A21/A22/A23 to roughly three quarters leading into A24/A25/A26, while the upstream A19→A20 step is stable (A19 before A20 in essentially all traces in both windows). [REL014, REL017, REL024, REL027, DIR020, REL013]
- The two blocks are alternatives in both windows (they co-occur in at most about 2 in 100 traces), and each still runs as a group of three: A21–A23 together in 75 in 100 traces before vs 25 in 100 after; A24–A26 together in 25 in 100 before vs 76 in 100 after. Both blocks precede A30. [REL036, REL044, REL051, REL058, REL059, REL064, REL040, REL061]
- A06 changes strongly: it runs in about 53 in 100 traces in the later window, up from about 17 in 100 (34→105 traces). Earlier it sat at varied, mostly early-to-middle positions (median relative position about 0.48); later it sits almost always at the end of the trace (median about 0.96), and its outgoing transitions, previously spread over A05, A07 and A09, now go to A35 in about 90 in 100 cases. [OCC006, POS001, DIR006]
- The later A06 occurrences sit between A34 and A35: A34 precedes A06 in about 46 in 100 traces (about 2 in 100 before), A06 precedes A35 in about 49 in 100 (about 17 in 100 before), about half of A34's outgoing transitions now lead to A06 (previously almost none), and the direct A34→A35 step (lag 1 in 90 in 100 cases before) is now split roughly half lag 1, half lag 2 — consistent with A06 being inserted between the two on about half of the traces. A06 also now typically runs after the A24–A26 block (A24 before A06 in about 36 in 100 traces vs about 1 in 100 before). [REL011, REL012, DIR034, LAG076, LAG005, REL006]
- Smaller shifts: A02, A04, A08 and A10 become rarer (e.g., A08 from about 14 in 100 to 5 in 100 traces), A15 and A16 repeat slightly more often, and after A30 the split moves from A31 toward A32. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC008, OCC010, OCC014, OCC015, DIR030, DIR032]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the routing after A19/A20 was changed: in the later window, cases that reach A19/A20 continue through A24, A25 and A26 (executed together, in varying order) in about three quarters of traces, where earlier they continued through A21, A22 and A23. Because both three-activity blocks are well observed and mutually exclusive in both windows, and the entry (A19→A20) and exit (toward A30) of the branch are stable, this reads as a shift in how often two existing alternative paths are taken rather than activities appearing or disappearing. The shift is large (about 50 in 100 traces per activity) and consistent across occurrence, direction and relation indicators. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the two windows simply sample different mixtures of pre-existing case variants at different rates, which would produce the same signature without any change to the routing itself. [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, REL014, REL017, REL024, REL027, DIR020, REL036, REL058, REL061]

Other differences:
- A06's new late role is a distinct, directly evidenced structural difference: in the later window A06 runs between A34 and A35 on about half of the traces, whereas earlier it appeared in about 17 in 100 traces at scattered early-to-middle positions with no dominant successor. [OCC006, POS001, DIR006, DIR034, REL011, REL012, LAG005, LAG076]
- A02, A04, A08 and A10 decline in participation (to roughly 5–8 in 100 traces), but each of these profiles rests on only about 10–36 observations per window, so these declines are weakly supported. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC008, OCC010]
- A15 and A16, present in every trace, show slightly more repetition (mean occurrences per trace about 1.73→1.83 and 1.74→1.84). [OCC014, OCC015]
- After A30, the branch split moves toward A32 (A30's outgoing transitions to A32 about 47→54 in 100, to A31 about 49→42 in 100), and A32 now leads to A33 in about 96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 82 in 100 before). [DIR030, DIR032]
